open_questions: Dates in ['Effective from (MM/DD/YYYY)'] could be day-first or month-first; read as day-first: confirm

notes: Source is a single CSV sheet ('prices', 13 rows incl. header, 9 columns); there is no inventory, category, promotion or brand sheet, so /inventory, /promotions, /category, /brand and /description are left unpopulated rather than guessed.

SKU values carry leading zeros (00470001-00470012) even though the profiler typed the column as int; the values must be read as text and kept with their zeros so /sku satisfies minLength 1 and preserves the customer identifier exactly.
Currency is an explicit 'USD' on every row; the schema default 'THB' is overridden by the source value and no FX conversion is performed, per the operator requirement.

Tax is explicit in the source: Tax included = 'No' (vat_included=false) and Tax rate = '5%' (vat_rate=0.05). The schema default vat_rate 0.07 is not applied because the file states its own rate; the 5% figure is treated as a fixture value as declared by the operator.

Effective from column header explicitly declares MM/DD/YYYY ordering, so 03/04/2026 resolves to 2026-03-04 without a date-format clarification. No effective_to / valid-until column exists, so /prices/*/effective_to stays null.
Sales unit 'PCS' is already a canonical value in the target enum_hint; no pack-size column exists, so /unit/pack_size stays null instead of being invented.

Status, barcode and description have no source columns; /status would take the schema default 'active' and barcode/description stay null — recorded as missing optional data, not as a blocking question.

tables.reason: Single flat sheet, one row per SKU (12 distinct SKUs, 12 rows), where the product identity columns (SKU, Product name) sit alongside a complete price-condition block: Currency, Sales unit, Price list, Net price, Tax included, Tax rate and Effective from. The dominant business payload is a per-SKU standard price with validity and tax condition, so the table role is pricing; SKU is the unique key that would join the price rows to products.

columns.name: SKU
columns.reason: Header 'SKU' matches the /sku synonym list exactly; 12 distinct values in 12 rows (unique_ratio 1.0) = product identity. Values are numeric-looking barcodes (00470001..00470012) with leading zeros, so the field must be read as text and zero-padded digits preserved, never cast to int.

columns.name: Product name
columns.reason: Header 'Product name' is a literal synonym of /product_name; values are human-readable item names ('SIM appliance 1'...) and are 100% distinct, one per SKU.

columns.name: Currency
columns.reason: Header 'Currency', single distinct explicit ISO code 'USD' on all rows. The ISO code is source evidence; it is used as-is with no FX conversion, and the schema default 'THB' must not override it.

columns.name: Sales unit
columns.reason: Header 'Sales unit' matches the unit.sell synonyms ('sales unit'); one distinct value 'PCS' which is already in the target enum_hint, so unit_normalize keeps it as PCS without any pack-size inference.

columns.name: Price list
columns.reason: Header 'Price list' matches the price.list_name synonyms; single distinct value 'standard', an explicitly supplied list name (not an inference), so it becomes the price_list of the single price condition per SKU.

columns.name: Net price
columns.reason: Header 'Net price' plus price_like hint, never null, 12 distinct values 1234.56-1356.77 with two decimals. This is the per-unit amount for the row's price condition; decimals are preserved exactly, no rounding applied.

columns.name: Tax included
columns.reason: Header 'Tax included' with values No/Yes semantics; the single distinct value is 'No' on all 12 rows, parsed via parse_bool to false. Value comes from the source, not from a retail convention, so the price is VAT-exclusive.

columns.name: Tax rate
columns.reason: Header 'Tax rate' with percent hint and literal value '5%' on every row — an explicit source tax rate, so parse_number_th(percent_to_fraction) gives 0.05 and this explicit rate takes precedence over the schema default 0.07. It is a fixture value, used only as written in the source.

columns.name: Effective from (MM/DD/YYYY)
columns.reason: Header 'Effective from' matches the effective_from synonyms and the parenthetical '(MM/DD/YYYY)' states the source order, so the ambiguous value 03/04/2026 is parsed dayfirst=false as month/day/year = 2026-03-04. Single distinct value, all rows, no end date supplied.

changes_from_draft: /sku now uses cast(trim(SKU), to string) with confidence 0.95 so the zero-padded identifiers '00470001'..'00470012' are emitted as text, per the operator requirement to preserve leading zeros; the draft's bare trim left the type at the profiler's int reading.

/prices/*/price_list is now read from the source column 'Price list' (normalize_whitespace) instead of the constant 'standard' — the file states the list name explicitly on every row, so no constant is needed.

Added /prices/*/vat_rate mapped from 'Tax rate' via parse_number_th(percent_to_fraction) → 0.05; the draft dropped this column as unmatched, but it is an explicit source tax rate and overrides the schema default 0.07.

/prices/*/vat_included now derives from the source flag 'Tax included' via parse_bool with default(false) rather than a bare constant, keeping the source evidence visible while 'No' on all rows yields false.

Added /prices/*/effective_from from 'Effective from (MM/DD/YYYY)' parsed with dayfirst=false, because the header itself declares month-first order; the draft's date-order question is resolved by the source header, so no clarification is raised.
/prices dedupe_keys set to the contract identity keys ['/price_list','/effective_from'] and record dedupe keyed on /sku, matching the schema identity keys.
Tightened quality rules: /sku not_null+unique (error), /currency regex ^[A-Z]{3}$, amount positive as error, vat_rate range 0–1 as warning.

Unpopulated optional fields recorded as information, not questions: /unit/pack_size (no pack-size column), /prices/*/effective_to (no valid-to column), /status (no status column — schema default 'active' applies), /barcode, /description, /brand, /category, /inventory and /promotions have no source data in this single CSV and are left unmapped rather than fabricated.
Currency 'USD' is taken verbatim from the file with no FX conversion; the schema default 'THB' is not applied.
